key_insight: CamPilot improves camera controllability in video diffusion models by introducing an efficient camera-aware reward feedback loop that evaluates and optimizes camera-video alignment without expensive RGB decoding.
problem_solved: Current reward-feedback approaches cannot reliably measure video-camera alignment and are computationally costly because they require decoding latents to RGB for reward computation; CamPilot addresses both accuracy and efficiency.
method: Train a specialized camera-alignment reward model that directly assesses camera trajectory fidelity with respect to prompts/targets.
Compute rewards in latent space (or via lightweight representations) to avoid repeated expensive decoding from latents to RGB during feedback loops.
Integrate the camera reward into a Reward Feedback Learning pipeline to fine-tune the video diffusion model for stronger, more precise camera control.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate videos with more accurate and controllable camera movements while reducing compute cost during optimization, making camera-conditioned video generation more practical for research and production.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt → diffusion model → latent video → camera-aware reward module (in-latent) → feedback loop for model update

paper_title: CamPilot: Improving Camera Control in Video Diffusion Model with Efficient Camera Reward Feedback
paper_authors: Wenhang Ge, Guibao Shen, Jiawei Feng, Luozhou Wang, Hao Lu
